NKJV.1: Then Joseph could not restrain himself before all those who stood by him, and he cried out, “Make everyone go out from me!” So no one stood with him while Joseph made himself known to his brothers.
NKJV.2: And he wept aloud, and the Egyptians and the house of Pharaoh heard it.
NKJV.3: Then Joseph said to his brothers, “I am Joseph; does my father still live?” But his brothers could not answer him, for they were dismayed in his presence.
NKJV.4: And Joseph said to his brothers, “Please come near to me.” So they came near. Then he said: “I am Joseph your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.
NKJV.5: But now, do not therefore be grieved or angry with yourselves because you sold me here; for God sent me before you to preserve life.
NKJV.6: For these two years the famine has been in the land, and there are still five years in which there will be neither plowing nor harvesting.
NKJV.7: And God sent me before you to preserve a posterity for you in the earth, and to save your lives by a great deliverance.
NKJV.8: So now it was not you who sent me here, but God; and He has made me a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and a ruler throughout all the land of Egypt.
NKJV.9: “Hurry and go up to my father, and say to him, ‘Thus says your son Joseph: “God has made me lord of all Egypt; come down to me, do not tarry.
NKJV.10: You shall dwell in the land of Goshen, and you shall be near to me, you and your children, your children’s children, your flocks and your herds, and all that you have.
NKJV.11: There I will provide for you, lest you and your household, and all that you have, come to poverty; for there are still five years of famine.” ’
NKJV.12: “And behold, your eyes and the eyes of my brother Benjamin see that it is my mouth that speaks to you.
NKJV.13: So you shall tell my father of all my glory in Egypt, and of all that you have seen; and you shall hurry and bring my father down here.”
NKJV.14: Then he fell on his brother Benjamin’s neck and wept, and Benjamin wept on his neck.
NKJV.15: Moreover he kissed all his brothers and wept over them, and after that his brothers talked with him.
NKJV.16: Now the report of it was heard in Pharaoh’s house, saying, “Joseph’s brothers have come.” So it pleased Pharaoh and his servants well.
NKJV.17: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Say to your brothers, ‘Do this: Load your animals and depart; go to the land of Canaan.
NKJV.18: Bring your father and your households and come to me; I will give you the best of the land of Egypt, and you will eat the fat of the land.
NKJV.19: Now you are commanded—do this: Take carts out of the land of Egypt for your little ones and your wives; bring your father and come.
NKJV.20: Also do not be concerned about your goods, for the best of all the land of Egypt is yours.’ ”
NKJV.21: Then the sons of Israel did so; and Joseph gave them carts, according to the command of Pharaoh, and he gave them provisions for the journey.
NKJV.22: He gave to all of them, to each man, changes of garments; but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of garments.
NKJV.23: And he sent to his father these things: ten donkeys loaded with the good things of Egypt, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain, bread, and food for his father for the journey.
NKJV.24: So he sent his brothers away, and they departed; and he said to them, “See that you do not become troubled along the way.”
NKJV.25: Then they went up out of Egypt, and came to the land of Canaan to Jacob their father.
NKJV.26: And they told him, saying, “Joseph is still alive, and he is governor over all the land of Egypt.” And Jacob’s heart stood still, because he did not believe them.
NKJV.27: But when they told him all the words which Joseph had said to them, and when he saw the carts which Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of Jacob their father revived.
NKJV.28: Then Israel said, “It is enough. Joseph my son is still alive. I will go and see him before I die.”

NASB.1: Then Joseph could not control himself before all those who stood by him, and he cried, 'Have everyone go out from me.' So there was no man with him when Joseph made himself known to his brothers.
NASB.2: He wept so loudly that the Egyptians heard [it], and the household of Pharaoh heard [of it].
NASB.3: Then Joseph said to his brothers, 'I am Joseph! Is my father still alive?' But his brothers could not answer him, for they were dismayed at his presence.
NASB.4: Then Joseph said to his brothers, 'Please come closer to me.' And they came closer. And he said, 'I am your brother Joseph, whom you sold into Egypt.
NASB.5: 'Now do not be grieved or angry with yourselves, because you sold me here, for God sent me before you to preserve life.
NASB.6: 'For the famine [has been] in the land these two years, and there are still five years in which there will be neither plowing nor harvesting.
NASB.7: 'God sent me before you to preserve for you a remnant in the earth, and to keep you alive by a great deliverance.
NASB.8: 'Now, therefore, it was not you who sent me here, but God; and He has made me a father to Pharaoh and lord of all his household and ruler over all the land of Egypt.
NASB.9: 'Hurry and go up to my father, and say to him, 'Thus says your son Joseph, 'God has made me lord of all Egypt; come down to me, do not delay.
NASB.10: 'You shall live in the land of Goshen, and you shall be near me, you and your children and your children's children and your flocks and your herds and all that you have.
NASB.11: 'There I will also provide for you, for there are still five years of famine [to come], and you and your household and all that you have would be impoverished.''
NASB.12: 'Behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin [see], that it is my mouth which is speaking to you.
NASB.13: 'Now you must tell my father of all my splendor in Egypt, and all that you have seen; and you must hurry and bring my father down here.'
NASB.14: Then he fell on his brother Benjamin's neck and wept, and Benjamin wept on his neck.
NASB.15: He kissed all his brothers and wept on them, and afterward his brothers talked with him.
NASB.16: Now when the news was heard in Pharaoh's house that Joseph's brothers had come, it pleased Pharaoh and his servants.
NASB.17: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, 'Say to your brothers, 'Do this: load your beasts and go to the land of Canaan,
NASB.18: and take your father and your households and come to me, and I will give you the best of the land of Egypt and you will eat the fat of the land.'
NASB.19: 'Now you are ordered, 'Do this: take wagons from the land of Egypt for your little ones and for your wives, and bring your father and come.
NASB.20: 'Do not concern yourselves with your goods, for the best of all the land of Egypt is yours.''
NASB.21: Then the sons of Israel did so; and Joseph gave them wagons according to the command of Pharaoh, and gave them provisions for the journey.
NASB.22: To each of them he gave changes of garments, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred [pieces of] silver and five changes of garments.
NASB.23: To his father he sent as follows: ten donkeys loaded with the best things of Egypt, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain and bread and sustenance for his father on the journey.
NASB.24: So he sent his brothers away, and as they departed, he said to them, 'Do not quarrel on the journey.'
NASB.25: Then they went up from Egypt, and came to the land of Canaan to their father Jacob.
NASB.26: They told him, saying, 'Joseph is still alive, and indeed he is ruler over all the land of Egypt.' But he was stunned, for he did not believe them.
NASB.27: When they told him all the words of Joseph that he had spoken to them, and when he saw the wagons that Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of their father Jacob revived.
NASB.28: Then Israel said, 'It is enough; my son Joseph is still alive. I will go and see him before I die.'

ESV.1: Then Joseph could not control himself before all those who stood by him. He cried, “Make everyone go out from me.” So no one stayed with him when Joseph made himself known to his brothers.
ESV.2: And he wept aloud, so that the Egyptians heard it, and the household of Pharaoh heard it.
ESV.3: And Joseph said to his brothers, “I am Joseph! Is my father still alive?” But his brothers could not answer him, for they were dismayed at his presence.
ESV.4: So Joseph said to his brothers, “Come near to me, please.” And they came near. And he said, “I am your brother, Joseph, whom you sold into Egypt.
ESV.5: And now do not be distressed or angry with yourselves because you sold me here, for God sent me before you to preserve life.
ESV.6: For the famine has been in the land these two years, and there are yet five years in which there will be neither plowing nor harvest.
ESV.7: And God sent me before you to preserve for you a remnant on earth, and to keep alive for you many survivors.
ESV.8: So it was not you who sent me here, but God. He has made me a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house and ruler over all the land of Egypt.
ESV.9: Hurry and go up to my father and say to him, ‘Thus says your son Joseph, God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me; do not tarry.
ESV.10: You shall dwell in the land of Goshen, and you shall be near me, you and your children and your children's children, and your flocks, your herds, and all that you have.
ESV.11: There I will provide for you, for there are yet five years of famine to come, so that you and your household, and all that you have, do not come to poverty.’
ESV.12: And now your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin see, that it is my mouth that speaks to you.
ESV.13: You must tell my father of all my honor in Egypt, and of all that you have seen. Hurry and bring my father down here.”
ESV.14: Then he fell upon his brother Benjamin's neck and wept, and Benjamin wept upon his neck.
ESV.15: And he kissed all his brothers and wept upon them. After that his brothers talked with him.
ESV.16: When the report was heard in Pharaoh's house, “Joseph's brothers have come,” it pleased Pharaoh and his servants.
ESV.17: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Say to your brothers, ‘Do this: load your beasts and go back to the land of Canaan,
ESV.18: and take your father and your households, and come to me, and I will give you the best of the land of Egypt, and you shall eat the fat of the land.’
ESV.19: And you, Joseph, are commanded to say, ‘Do this: take wagons from the land of Egypt for your little ones and for your wives, and bring your father, and come.
ESV.20: Have no concern for  your goods, for the best of all the land of Egypt is yours.’”
ESV.21: The sons of Israel did so: and Joseph gave them wagons, according to the command of Pharaoh, and gave them provisions for the journey.
ESV.22: To each and all of them he gave a change of clothes, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred shekels  of silver and five changes of clothes.
ESV.23: To his father he sent as follows: ten donkeys loaded with the good things of Egypt, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain, bread, and provision for his father on the journey.
ESV.24: Then he sent his brothers away, and as they departed, he said to them, “Do not quarrel on the way.”
ESV.25: So they went up out of Egypt and came to the land of Canaan to their father Jacob.
ESV.26: And they told him, “Joseph is still alive, and he is ruler over all the land of Egypt.” And his heart became numb, for he did not believe them.
ESV.27: But when they told him all the words of Joseph, which he had said to them, and when he saw the wagons that Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of their father Jacob revived.
ESV.28: And Israel said, “It is enough; Joseph my son is still alive. I will go and see him before I die.”

NLT.1: Joseph could stand it no longer. There were many people in the room, and he said to his attendants, “Out, all of you!” So he was alone with his brothers when he told them who he was.
NLT.2: Then he broke down and wept. He wept so loudly the Egyptians could hear him, and word of it quickly carried to Pharaoh’s palace.
NLT.3: “I am Joseph!” he said to his brothers. “Is my father still alive?” But his brothers were speechless! They were stunned to realize that Joseph was standing there in front of them.
NLT.4: “Please, come closer,” he said to them. So they came closer. And he said again, “I am Joseph, your brother, whom you sold into slavery in Egypt.
NLT.5: But don’t be upset, and don’t be angry with yourselves for selling me to this place. It was God who sent me here ahead of you to preserve your lives.
NLT.6: This famine that has ravaged the land for two years will last five more years, and there will be neither plowing nor harvesting.
NLT.7: God has sent me ahead of you to keep you and your families alive and to preserve many survivors.
NLT.8: So it was God who sent me here, not you! And he is the one who made me an adviser to Pharaoh — the manager of his entire palace and the governor of all Egypt.
NLT.9: “Now hurry back to my father and tell him, ‘This is what your son Joseph says: God has made me master over all the land of Egypt. So come down to me immediately!
NLT.10: You can live in the region of Goshen, where you can be near me with all your children and grandchildren, your flocks and herds, and everything you own.
NLT.11: I will take care of you there, for there are still five years of famine ahead of us. Otherwise you, your household, and all your animals will starve.’”
NLT.12: Then Joseph added, “Look! You can see for yourselves, and so can my brother Benjamin, that I really am Joseph!
NLT.13: Go tell my father of my honored position here in Egypt. Describe for him everything you have seen, and then bring my father here quickly.”
NLT.14: Weeping with joy, he embraced Benjamin, and Benjamin did the same.
NLT.15: Then Joseph kissed each of his brothers and wept over them, and after that they began talking freely with him.
NLT.16: The news soon reached Pharaoh’s palace: “Joseph’s brothers have arrived!” Pharaoh and his officials were all delighted to hear this.
NLT.17: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Tell your brothers, ‘This is what you must do: Load your pack animals, and hurry back to the land of Canaan.
NLT.18: Then get your father and all of your families, and return here to me. I will give you the very best land in Egypt, and you will eat from the best that the land produces.’”
NLT.19: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Tell your brothers, ‘Take wagons from the land of Egypt to carry your little children and your wives, and bring your father here.
NLT.20: Don’t worry about your personal belongings, for the best of all the land of Egypt is yours.’”
NLT.21: So the sons of Jacob did as they were told. Joseph provided them with wagons, as Pharaoh had commanded, and he gave them supplies for the journey.
NLT.22: And he gave each of them new clothes — but to Benjamin he gave five changes of clothes and 300 pieces of silver.
NLT.23: He also sent his father ten male donkeys loaded with the finest products of Egypt, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain and bread and other supplies he would need on his journey.
NLT.24: So Joseph sent his brothers off, and as they left, he called after them, “Don’t quarrel about all this along the way!”
NLT.25: And they left Egypt and returned to their father, Jacob, in the land of Canaan.
NLT.26: “Joseph is still alive!” they told him. “And he is governor of all the land of Egypt!” Jacob was stunned at the news — he couldn’t believe it.
NLT.27: But when they repeated to Jacob everything Joseph had told them, and when he saw the wagons Joseph had sent to carry him, their father’s spirits revived.
NLT.28: Then Jacob exclaimed, “It must be true! My son Joseph is alive! I must go and see him before I die.”

CSB17.1: Joseph could no longer keep his composure in front of all his attendants, <sup>[1]</sup> so he called out, “Send everyone away from me!” No one was with him when he revealed his identity to his brothers. <sup>ⓛ</sup>

CSB17.3: Joseph said to his brothers, “I am Joseph! Is my father still living?” But they could not answer him because they were terrified in his presence.
CSB17.4: Then Joseph said to his brothers, “Please, come near me,” and they came near. “I am Joseph, your brother,” he said, “the one you sold into Egypt. <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.5: And now don’t be grieved or angry with yourselves for selling me here, because God sent me ahead of you to preserve life. <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.6: For the famine has been in the land these two years, and there will be five more years without plowing or harvesting.
CSB17.7: God sent me ahead of you to establish you as a remnant within the land and to keep you alive by a great deliverance. <sup>[2]</sup>

CSB17.9: “Return quickly to my father and say to him, ‘This is what your son Joseph says: “God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me without delay.

CSB17.11: There I will sustain you, for there will be five more years of famine. Otherwise, you, your household, and everything you have will become destitute.”’ <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.12: Look! Your eyes and the eyes of my brother Benjamin can see that I’m <sup>[3]</sup> the one speaking to you.
CSB17.13: Tell my father about all my glory in Egypt and about all you have seen. And bring my father here quickly.” <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.14: Then Joseph threw his arms around his brother Benjamin and wept, and Benjamin wept on his shoulder.
CSB17.15: Joseph kissed each of his brothers as he wept, <sup>[4]</sup> and afterward his brothers talked with him.
CSB17.16: When the news reached Pharaoh’s palace, “Joseph’s brothers have come,” Pharaoh and his servants were pleased.
CSB17.17: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Tell your brothers, ‘Do this: Load your animals and go on back to the land of Canaan.
CSB17.18: Get your father and your families, and come back to me. I will give you the best of the land of Egypt, and you can eat from the richness of the land.’
CSB17.19: You are also commanded to tell them, ‘Do this: Take wagons from the land of Egypt for your dependents and your wives and bring your father here. <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.20: Do not be concerned about your belongings, for the best of all the land of Egypt is yours.’” <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.21: The sons of Israel did this. Joseph gave them wagons as Pharaoh had commanded, and he gave them provisions for the journey.
CSB17.22: He gave each of the brothers changes of clothes, <sup>ⓕ</sup> but he gave Benjamin three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of clothes. <sup>ⓖ</sup>
CSB17.23: He sent his father the following: ten donkeys carrying the best products of Egypt and ten female donkeys carrying grain, food, and provisions for his father on the journey.
CSB17.24: So Joseph sent his brothers on their way, and as they were leaving, he said to them, “Don’t argue <sup>[5]</sup> on the way.”
CSB17.25: So they went up from Egypt and came to their father Jacob in the land of Canaan.
CSB17.26: They said, “Joseph is still alive, and he is ruler over all the land of Egypt!” Jacob was stunned, <sup>[6]</sup> for he did not believe them.

AMP.1: Then Joseph could not control himself [any longer] in front of all those who attended him, and he called out, "Have everyone leave me." So no man stood there when Joseph revealed himself to his brothers.
AMP.2: Joseph wept aloud, and the Egyptians [who had just left him] heard it, and the household of Pharaoh heard of it.
AMP.3: Then Joseph said to his brothers, "I am Joseph! Is my father still alive?" But his brothers were speechless, for they were stunned and dismayed by [the fact that they were in] Joseph's presence.
AMP.4: And Joseph said to his brothers, "Please come closer to me." And they approached him. And he said, "I am Joseph your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.
AMP.5: Now do not be distressed or angry with yourselves because you sold me here, for God sent me ahead of you to save life and preserve our family.
AMP.6: For the famine has been in the land these two years, and there are still five more years in which there will be no plowing and harvesting.
AMP.7: God sent me [to Egypt] ahead of you to preserve for you a remnant on the earth, and to keep you alive by a great escape.
AMP.8: So now it was not you who sent me here, but God; and He has made me a father to Pharaoh and lord of all his household and ruler over all the land of Egypt.
AMP.9: Hurry and go up to my father, and tell him, 'Your son Joseph says this to you: "God has made me lord of all Egypt; come down to me, do not delay.
AMP.10: You shall live in the land of Goshen [the best pasture land of Egypt], and you shall be close to me—you and your children and your grandchildren, your flocks and your herds and all you have.
AMP.11: There I will provide for you and sustain you, so that you and your household and all that are yours may not become impoverished, for there are still five years of famine to come."'
AMP.12: Look! Your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin see, that I am speaking to you [personally in your language and not through an interpreter].
AMP.13: Now you must tell my father of all my splendor and power in Egypt, and of everything that you have seen; and you must hurry and bring my father down here."
AMP.14: Then he embraced his brother Benjamin's neck and wept, and Benjamin wept on his neck.
AMP.15: He kissed all his brothers and wept on them, and afterward his brothers talked with him.
AMP.16: When the news was heard in Pharaoh's house that Joseph's brothers had come, it pleased Pharaoh and his servants.
AMP.17: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Tell your brothers, 'Do this: load your animals and return to the land of Canaan [without delay],
AMP.18: and get your father and your households and come to me. I will give you the best of the land of Egypt and you will eat the fat (the finest produce) of the land.'
AMP.19: Now you [brothers of Joseph] are ordered [by Pharaoh], 'Do this: take wagons from the land of Egypt for your little ones and for your wives, and bring your father and come.
AMP.20: Do not be concerned with your goods, for the best of all the land of Egypt is yours.'"
AMP.21: Then the sons of Israel did so; and Joseph gave them wagons according to the command of Pharaoh, and gave them provisions for the journey.
AMP.22: To each of them Joseph gave changes of clothing, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of clothing.
AMP.23: To his father he sent the following: ten male donkeys loaded with the good things of Egypt, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain and bread and provision for his father [to supply all who were with him] on the journey.
AMP.24: So he sent his brothers away, and as they departed, he said to them, "See that you do not quarrel on the journey [about how to explain this to our father]."
AMP.25: So they went up from Egypt, and came to the land of Canaan to Jacob their father,
AMP.26: and they said to him, "Joseph is still alive, and indeed he is ruler over all the land of Egypt." But Jacob was stunned and his heart almost stopped beating, because he did not believe them.

AMP.28: And Israel (Jacob) said, "It is enough! Joseph my son is still alive. I will go and see him before I die."

MSG.1: Joseph couldn't hold himself in any longer, keeping up a front before all his attendants. He cried out, "Leave! Clear out—everyone leave!" So there was no one with Joseph when he identified himself to his brothers.
MSG.2: But his sobbing was so violent that the Egyptians couldn't help but hear him. The news was soon reported to Pharaoh's palace.
MSG.3: Joseph spoke to his brothers: "I am Joseph. Is my father really still alive?" But his brothers couldn't say a word. They were speechless—they couldn't believe what they were hearing and seeing.

MSG.5: But don't feel badly, don't blame yourselves for selling me. God was behind it. God sent me here ahead of you to save lives.
